report.question: Does reducing phosphorus change chlorophyll-a in lakes?

cited_evidence.text: In a synthetic randomized intervention, a phosphorus reduction changes chlorophyll-a, but the result does not estimate any real lake effect.
In an illustrative observational record, phosphorus and chlorophyll-a are positively associated. No causal experiment was performed.
A synthetic example shows phosphorus decreasing but chlorophyll-a staying high during a period of elevated temperature.
An illustrative causal diagram considers land use and temperature as confounders of the phosphorus and chlorophyll-a association.
A hypothetical lake management study reports phosphorus declining after a planned intervention, followed by lower chlorophyll-a under stable weather.
